items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: Leonard Parker was out of Slide Hill, I played with him quite a while.

ctx.x: Never heard, he's the best you ever heard in your whole life, you mean any place, huh?

Any place. Any place. And uh, they had a real, real good band. And there was uh, Leonard Parker around there, there was Tommy Ladner. Leonard Parker was out of Slide Hill, I played with him quite a while. And then Dan Moody, during that time Dan was playing uh, trombone instead of, and he got off the trombone and went, got back on the bass violin.
Who was that foul singer over there, Black Eagle?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: the first band I saw use music over there was Leonard Parker's band. And then Parker was a good spell a little bit and he used to, I saw him with music.

ctx.x: I never saw any music. I never saw no band use any music except, the first band I saw use music over there was Leonard Parker's band. And then Parker was a good spell a little bit and he used to, I saw him with music. But the rest of them I never saw anyone with no music. And then also René used to come over there with Morris French and Morris French's brother with the tuba, playing the tuba at the different time, used to come over there and they wrote it.
